question.text: If $\vec{a}+\vec{b}=\vec{c}$ and $a+b=c$, then the angle included between $\vec{a}$ and $\vec{b}$ is

solution.text:
Hints: Here $\vec{a}+\vec{b}=\vec{c} \& c=a+b$
Now, $c=\sqrt{a^2+b^2+2 a b \cos \theta}$
$\begin{aligned}
& (a+b)=\sqrt{a^2+b^2+2 a b \cos \theta} \\
& a^2+b^2+2 a b=a^2+b^2+2 a b \cos \theta \\
& \cos \theta=1, \theta=0^{\circ}
\end{aligned}$
